model.name: LunchBox — Technology Layer
model.documentation: Technology layer view of LunchBox as of 2026-09-20. Deliberately scoped to infrastructure/runtime elements only (Nodes, System Software, Artifacts, Technology Services) — application-level logic (services/hooks/components, the chat tool-calling loop) belongs in a separate Application layer model, realized on top of this one.

element.name: User's Browser
element.documentation: Runs the compiled React SPA. School admin/staff client device.

element.name: Vercel Serverless Platform
element.documentation: Hosts the static SPA build and the api/**.js serverless functions. Auto-deploys from GitHub on push.

element.name: Node.js Runtime
element.documentation: ESM-module runtime executing the api/ serverless functions.

element.name: LunchBox SPA Bundle
element.documentation: Vite/React production build (npm run build), deployed as static assets.

element.name: api/chat/execute.js (deployed function)
element.documentation: The confirm-gated write-execution endpoint — the only place a chat-originated write actually happens.

element.name: Supabase Platform
element.documentation: Managed backend platform hosting Postgres, Auth, and Storage for LunchBox.

element.name: PostgreSQL (+ pgvector planned)
element.documentation: Primary datastore. Row Level Security (RLS) is the multi-tenant isolation mechanism for every table. pgvector extension planned for the policy-document RAG feature.

element.name: Supabase Auth (GoTrue)
element.documentation: Issues the JWTs that both the browser client and the chat backend use — the chat backend forwards the caller's own JWT rather than using a service-role key, so RLS enforces tenant isolation identically for both.

element.name: Local Developer Machine
element.documentation: Runs the MCP stdio server and the local dev-server.js Express shim (dev-only proxy for testing api/ functions before Vercel deployment).

element.name: mcp_server/server.js
element.documentation: Local-only stdio MCP server, 27 tools, connects to Claude Desktop. Single-tenant per process (hardcoded SCHOOL_ID) — never internet-facing.

element.name: Anthropic Messages API
element.documentation: External. Powers the chat tool-calling loop and the future RAG answer synthesis. Billed separately (prepaid credits, no auto-reload).

element.name: Voyage AI Embeddings API
element.documentation: External — planned, not yet built. Text-to-vector conversion for the policy-document RAG feature; stateless, no storage on the vendor side.

relationship.documentation: Serves the SPA bundle and API responses over HTTPS.
Every query — browser-direct or via the chat backend — is scoped through the calling user's own JWT, never a service-role key, so RLS enforces tenant isolation identically for both paths.
MCP server uses the service-role key (bypasses RLS) — single-tenant per process, local-only, never internet-facing.
Planned — RAG feature not yet built.
